record.provider: WeChat Official Account — uploadimg (图文消息图片, the uncapped endpoint)

free_tier.stated: NO documented count cap. The docs state explicitly: "该接口所上传的图片，不占用公众号的素材库中图片数量的100000个的限制". Images uploaded via this endpoint do NOT count against the 100,000-image library limit. Per-file cap 1 MB, JPG/PNG only.

retention.stated: | Images are permanent in practice (they must survive in published articles forever), but the service is tuned for article inline images, so bulk non-image binary upload is impossible and a hotlink-blocked 403 can appear without warning.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered. The response hands back a public CDN URL on mmbiz.qpic.cn ("url": "http://mmbiz.qpic.cn/XXXXX"), which is served by Tencent's CDN with no access_token and no auth header. This is the only genuinely anonymous read path found in this entire slot.

record.tooling: Trivial. One multipart POST: curl -F media=@test.jpg "https://api.weixin.qq.com/cgi-bin/media/uploadimg?access_token=ACCESS_TOKEN". No wrapper needed; any HTTP client plus a token-refresh loop (access_token lives 7200s) is the whole client.
record.chaining: The absence of a count cap means one account is already unbounded in object count; the binding limit becomes 1 MB/file. 1 account = effectively millions of 1MB objects. Multiple Official Accounts (1 per entity) multiply further, but count is not the constraint. File size is.
record.limits_note: 1 MB per image, jpg/png only. access_token required to UPLOAD (2h expiry, refresh loop needed). Download is anonymous. mmbiz.qpic.cn applies a Referer/hotlink check. Direct GETs without a WeChat/weixin Referer can be refused, which breaks plain curl fetch fan-out and CDN-fronting.
record.reliability_note: Images are permanent in practice (they must survive in published articles forever), but the service is tuned for article inline images, so bulk non-image binary upload is impossible and a hotlink-blocked 403 can appear without warning.
